Complete Local Interpretation Pipeline

Source: R/kumquat.R
kumquat.Rd

Runs the LIME pipeline for each point of interest: generate perturbations, predict them with the black-box model, weight them, and fit a local surrogate. Each step is carried out by a function that can be replaced through perturb_fun, weight_fun and surrogate_fun.

Usage

kumquat(
  model_bundle,
  data,
  pois,
  perturbations = NULL,
  radius = 0.1,
  step = 0.01,
  predictor_vars = c("x", "y"),
  nfolds = 50,
  alpha = 1,
  class_names = c("A", "B"),
  predict_func = stats::predict,
  weighted = FALSE,
  kernel_width = NULL,
  dist_fun = "euclidean",
  perturb_fun = generate_perturbations,
  weight_fun = NULL,
  surrogate_fun = fit_local_model
)

Arguments

model_bundle

A trained model held in a bundle::bundle()

data

Training data

pois

Points of interest (data rows)

perturbations

A list of data.frames of perturbations, one per point of interest, to be used instead of calling perturb_fun

radius

Perturbation radius (default: 0.1)

step

Perturbation step size (default: 0.01)

predictor_vars

Character vector of predictor variable names

nfolds

Number of CV folds (default: 50)

alpha

Elastic net parameter (default: 1)

class_names

Class names passed to fit_local_model(); only used to label numeric (0/1) predictions

predict_func

A function that takes in two arguments: model and data and returns a vector of factors

weighted

If TRUE, weight perturbations by their proximity to the point of interest using weight_fun when fitting the local model, as in LIME (default: FALSE). Ignored when weight_fun is supplied.

kernel_width

Kernel width passed to weight_fun

dist_fun

Distance measure passed to weight_fun

perturb_fun

Function that generates the perturbations around a point of interest (default: generate_perturbations()).

weight_fun

Function that weights the perturbations. If NULL (default), kernel_weights() is used when weighted = TRUE and all perturbations are weighted equally otherwise. Supplying a function always weights the perturbations.

surrogate_fun

Function that fits the local surrogate model (default: fit_local_model()).

Value

A list with one element per point of interest, each containing perturbations, local_model, point_of_interest and train_data.

Replacing steps

Each step function is called with named arguments. A replacement only needs to accept the arguments it uses: arguments that are not in its formals are dropped, unless it has a ... argument, in which case all are passed.

  • perturb_fun is called with data, poi (a single-row data frame), radius, step, predictors and predictor_vars (both are the predictor names). It must return a data frame containing the predictor_vars columns, one row per perturbation.

  • weight_fun is called with perturbations (including the black-box predictions in column pred), poi, predictor_vars, kernel_width and dist_fun. It must return a numeric vector with one non-negative weight per perturbation.

  • surrogate_fun is called with perturbations (including pred), predictor_vars, nfolds, alpha, class_names and weights (NULL when the perturbations are not weighted). It must return a list. To work with plot_interest() and pinch_importance(), it should contain glm_predictions (one predicted class per perturbation) and importances (a named numeric vector).

Examples

data(d_vertical)
rfmodel <- randomForest::randomForest(
 class ~ x + y,
 data = d_vertical
)
# Bundle model up
rfmodel_bundled <- bundle::bundle(rfmodel)
ks <- kumquat(
 rfmodel_bundled,
 d_vertical,
  d_vertical[1,],
  class_names = unique(d_vertical$class)
)
#> INFO [2026-11-19 03:36:49] Picking kumquats for row: 1

# Replace the perturbation step with uniform random sampling in the box
random_box <- function(poi, radius, predictor_vars) {
  n <- 500
  as.data.frame(lapply(
    stats::setNames(predictor_vars, predictor_vars),
    \(v) stats::runif(n, poi[[v]] - radius, poi[[v]] + radius)
  ))
}
ks_random <- kumquat(
  rfmodel_bundled,
  d_vertical,
  d_vertical[799, ],
  class_names = levels(d_vertical$class),
  perturb_fun = random_box
)
#> INFO [2026-11-19 03:36:49] Picking kumquats for row: 1
